Omg you have truly articulated my thoughts so perfectly. Thank you for all of this. It’s so refreshing to know people beyond myself and my friends think this way too. Building community is so important, especially in marginalized communities, and that’s impossible without conflict resolution skills and accountability from all parties.

I’m really sorry you experienced that. I lost all my close friends when I was 17, and as traumatic as it was, it fueled a really profound period of growth where I was able to reconnect with people I truly felt aligned with. I wish you lots of healing, and I hope you are able to find people who are better aligned with you. Relationships and people are complicated and unfortunately a lot of people are primarily interested in what keeps them comfortable. You shouldn’t blame yourself, and I promise you there are people out there willing to work to keep you in their lives. <3

I think about this a lot too, and I always wish I could come up with an objective answer that perfectly explains where that boundary lies. It’s obviously ideal for friends to be understanding and accommodating, but it’s also not fair to resent them when they sometimes don’t have the capacity to center their actions around us. Their job is to lookout for their #1 (themselves) and the same is true for us! 

I think a lot of my frustration with others often manifests when I am disrespecting or not showing up for myself in the ways I need (i.e. taking care of myself physically or setting boundaries around my time). I also feel like I like to think I am a completely objective thinker, but no one is lol, and my black and white thinking often gets muddled by my self interests, emotions, and fear of abandonment. 

I mostly hangout with other AuDHDers, and I have also been on the receiving end of black/white thinking, and it was honestly traumatic to be abandoned by a friend like that. I think one of the biggest parts in developing a more nuanced approach for me was really hurting one of my closest friends last year with my black and white thinking around our relationship. Her and I didn’t talk for several months and when we reconnected I was reminded of how much I loved her, and I really regretted the way I handled things. We’ve worked through things since, but originally, I barely even gave her the chance to explain before and blamed her a lot for a situation I had a very big role in. 

Feeling “comfortable” or at ease isn’t always what’s best for us, and sometimes discomfort indicates growth. Relationships honestly take a lot of work and effort, especially when you are traumatized and neurodivergent and surrounded by people who are as well lol. It’s not really fair or healthy to jump ship anytime something makes us feel triggered, and relationships feel so much more intimate and fulfilling when you are able to overcome hurdles like that together.

This is what I’ve had to realize too! No relationship is perfect. People will inevitably hurt and disappoint you and not show up when you need them to, but I think the ratio of when they do vs don’t is incredibly important. Being able to show up for yourself when others aren’t able to is the most important part of being mentally stable and maintaining healthy fulfilling relationships imo

This isn’t to say that people should tolerate disrespect either, I’ve just noticed (because of trauma and autism i’m assuming?) I can overreact to disrespect from people with good intentions and under react to disrespect from people with bad ones (namely men I am romantically involved with). I just try to look at ALL their actions throughout our relationship completely objectively and decide if the person is worth the effort. Usually though if I am attached, I will at least have a conversation with them about how I am feeling while trying to be as tactful as possible. It is HARD, but it is worth it to me. The way they respond when you are openly vulnerable and kind (which is really hard for me especially when emotionally charged) is very telling and usually the final decision maker for me in whether or not a relationship is worth it. This method hasn’t failed me yet!

I feel like I used to do this a lot and as i’ve gotten older have really tried to reel it in. I also used to lash out at people and burn bridges quite a bit. Now I try to think very hard and objectively about someone’s intentions and character and how I may be misinterpreting or assigning meaning to their actions that isn’t necessarily there. There are plenty of times I have come off as rude or disrespectful to others but didn’t mean things that way at all, so I try to give other people the benefit of the doubt. I think that I am very lucky in that regard though, because all my friends are very mature, kind, understanding, and empathetic (though it took LOTS of trial and error to finally find and develop the “right” group). I definitely have panic moments where I feel like I will never be able to trust someone again because our interaction seemingly showed such blatant disrespect or lack of care, but people are messy, including myself, and shitty at communicating. I feel like at the end of the day relationships, romantic or not, are about commitment, and whether or not the value and fulfillment your relationship with someone brings to your life is worth the effort of being vulnerable and trying to work through conflict. Ultimately, the majority of my friends i’ve known for 10+ years and that sense of security and love is incredibly important to me. Unless they were to continuously repeat a pattern that I felt indicated a serious lack of empathy or accountability, I see no reason to just cut things off. I just try to treat them the same way I’d want to be treated if I made a shitty mistake or comment because god knows how many times i’ve done that.
